ai.literal: Companion-goodness prosperity will give; action-goodness desired all will give.
ai.translation: Having good companions brings prosperity, but the purity of one's actions will yield everything desired.
ai.modern: நல்ல துணையை அடைந்திருப்பது ஒருவனுக்குச் செல்வத்தைத் தரும்; ஆனால் செய்யும் செயலின் தூய்மையானது அவன் விரும்பிய எல்லாவற்றையும் அவனுக்குத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the benefits of good associations with the benefits of pure actions. The phrase 'துணைநலம்' refers to having good and supportive companions, which brings material prosperity. However, 'வினைநலம்', which means the goodness or purity of one's own actions, is far more powerful. Pure actions will yield absolutely everything a person desires, showing that righteous conduct is the ultimate source of fulfillment.

ai.literal: Always abandoning is necessary, with fame good not-yielding action.
ai.translation: One must always abandon actions that do not yield goodness and fame.
ai.modern: புகழையும் நன்மையையும் தராத செயல்களை ஒருவன் எப்போதும் தவிர்த்தல் வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet sets a clear standard for choosing one's actions. It states that any deed failing to produce both moral goodness and a good reputation must be strictly avoided. The word 'என்றும்' (always) emphasizes that there are no exceptions to this rule, regardless of the situation or potential short-term gains. By commanding 'ஒருவுதல் வேண்டும்' (must be abandoned), the text insists that pure conduct requires rejecting anything that compromises one's honor or virtue.

ai.literal: shunning is-needed glory fading doing-action 'we-will-prosper' who-say they
ai.translation: Those who say to themselves, 'We will prosper,' must shun actions that would dim their glory.
ai.modern: நாம் வாழ்வில் மேன்மை அடைவோம் என்று எண்ணுபவர்கள், தம் புகழைக் கெடுக்கும் செயல்களைச் செய்வதை விட்டுவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet advises ambitious individuals on the importance of pure actions. The word 'ஆஅதும்' (we will prosper) captures the mindset of those who wish to rise in life. To achieve true success, they must avoid 'ஒளி மாழ்கும் செய்வினை', which means actions that tarnish their 'ஒளி' (light or glory). Even if a bad action seems to offer a shortcut, it will ultimately destroy their reputation and must be strictly shunned ('ஓஒதல் வேண்டும்').

ai.literal: Distress even if experienced, disgraceful things they will not do, wavering-free vision those people.
ai.translation: Even if they fall into deep distress, those with unwavering vision will not commit disgraceful deeds.
ai.modern: துன்பம் வந்தாலும், நடுக்கம் இல்லாத தெளிவான அறிவை உடையவர்கள் இழிவான செயல்களைச் செய்ய மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the steadfastness of those with clear, unwavering understanding. The word 'இடுக்கண்' (distress) sets up a scenario of extreme hardship, which often tempts people to compromise their principles. However, 'நடுக்கற்ற காட்சி' (unwavering vision or clarity) gives them the strength to resist. Consequently, they will never do 'இளிவந்த' (disgraceful or degrading) deeds, maintaining the purity of their actions regardless of their circumstances.

ai.literal: 'What!' saying, things to regret do not do; if one does, again such things not doing is good.
ai.translation: Do not commit acts that will make you cry out, 'What have I done!' If you have made such a mistake, it is good to never repeat it.
ai.modern: 'இப்படிச் செய்துவிட்டேனே!' என்று வருந்தும்படியான செயல்களைச் செய்யக்கூடாது. ஒருவேளை தவறுதலாகச் செய்துவிட்டாலும், மீண்டும் அத்தகைய செயல்களைச் செய்யாமல் இருப்பதே நல்லது.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises against actions that lead to future remorse. The phrase 'எற்று என்று' captures the exclamation of a person regretting their own deed, wondering what they have done. The word 'இரங்குவ' refers to actions that bring such grief. The couplet adds a practical concession: if one happens to make such a mistake, the best course of action is to ensure it is never repeated. This emphasizes that purity of action involves both avoiding regrettable deeds and learning from mistakes.

ai.literal: Mother's hunger he who sees even if, let him not do noble ones condemning action.
ai.translation: Even if one has to see one's own mother starving, one must not do deeds that the noble condemn.
ai.modern: பெற்ற தாயின் பசியைக் காண நேர்ந்தாலும், சான்றோர்கள் பழிக்கும் தீய செயல்களை ஒருவன் செய்யக்கூடாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the absolute necessity of purity in action, regardless of the circumstances. The most extreme and emotionally compelling hardship one can face is seeing one's own mother suffer from hunger. Even in such a desperate situation, the text insists that one must not resort to actions condemned by the noble. The strong negative injunction 'செய்யற்க' leaves no room for exceptions, placing moral integrity above even the most fundamental human attachments.

ai.literal: Blame having incurred attained than wealth, noble ones' extreme poverty indeed superior.
ai.translation: The extreme poverty of the noble is far better than wealth attained by incurring disgrace.
ai.modern: பழியைச் சுமந்து பெற்ற செல்வத்தை விட, சான்றோர்கள் அடையும் கொடிய வறுமையே மிகவும் சிறந்தது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts two states: wealth gained through shameful actions and severe poverty endured by the noble. The word 'malainthu' means to take upon oneself or wear, illustrating how one wears disgrace like a burden to acquire such wealth. The text concludes that the extreme poverty ('kaḻi nalkuravu') of the virtuous is superior ('talai') to any prosperity bought at the cost of one's purity of action.

ai.literal: condemned things / having rejected / they shun not / to those who did / those things / themselves / even if accomplished / sorrow / will give
ai.translation: Even if successfully accomplished, forbidden actions done by those who fail to shun them will only bring sorrow.
ai.modern: விலக்கப்பட்ட தீய செயல்களை முழுமையாக விலக்காமல் செய்பவர்களுக்கு, அச்செயல்கள் வெற்றிகரமாக முடிந்தாலும் முடிவில் துன்பத்தையே தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against engaging in actions that are fundamentally wrong or forbidden. The phrase 'கடிந்த கடிந்து ஒரார்' refers to those who fail to reject and stay away from condemned deeds. Even if such impure actions seem to succeed and reach completion ('முடிந்தாலும்'), the actions themselves ('அவை தாம்') will ultimately yield only sorrow ('பீழை'). The emphasis is on the purity of action, showing that bad means cannot lead to truly good ends.

ai.literal: Weeping acquired all weeping will go; even if lost, later will yield things of good nature.
ai.translation: All that is acquired by making others weep will depart, making oneself weep. But things of a good nature, even if lost, will yield benefits later.
ai.modern: பிறர் அழும்படி தீய வழியில் சேர்த்தவை எல்லாம், தாமும் அழும்படி விட்டுப் போய்விடும். ஆனால் நல்ல வழியில் வந்தவை தற்காலிகமாக அழிந்தாலும், பின்பு நல்ல பலன்களையே தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts wealth gained through cruel means with wealth gained through righteous means. The word 'அழ' (weeping) is used twice to show a direct consequence: wealth acquired by causing tears will be lost in a way that brings tears to the acquirer. Conversely, 'நற்பாலவை' refers to things of a good, pure nature. Even if such good things are temporarily lost, they will eventually yield positive results.

ai.literal: By deceit wealth having accumulated feeling secure [is] unbaked clay inside vessel water having poured having kept like.
ai.translation: Feeling secure after accumulating wealth by deceitful means is like pouring and storing water in a vessel of unbaked clay.
ai.modern: வஞ்சனையான வழிகளில் பொருளைச் சேர்த்து வைத்துப் பாதுகாப்பாக உணர்வது, சுடப்படாத பச்சை மண்ணால் செய்த பானையில் நீரை ஊற்றி வைப்பதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against accumulating wealth through unethical or deceitful means. The word 'சலம்' refers to deceit or falseness. The poet compares such ill-gotten wealth to water poured into a vessel made of unbaked clay ('பசுமண் கலம்'). Just as the unbaked clay will dissolve and both the vessel and the water will be lost, wealth gained by deceit will inevitably destroy itself and its possessor.
